description.value: A randomized, single-blind, sham-controlled, crossover fMRI study examined how a single session of active versus sham rTMS over the left DLPFC affected cue-induced BOLD activity in non-treatment-seeking nicotine-dependent smokers.

spans.text: We conducted a randomized, single-blind, sham-controlled, crossover study in which participants received both active and sham rTMS over the left DLPFC, with a 1-week interval between treatments to avoid carryover effects.

value: Our hypothesis was that rTMS would reduce brain activity in the brain regions previously implicated in cigarette smoking craving and relapse (including mOFC, NAc and ventral striatum (VS)).
We additionally hypothesized that rTMS would increase cue-induced brain activity underneath the rTMS stimulation site (the DLPFC).

Cigarette smoking cue-induced fMRI paradigm

description.value: Participants viewed smoking-related, neutral, and rest visual cues and rated craving in the scanner.

spans.text: A 12-minute sequence for stimuli presentation consisted of eight, 90-second epochs presented after participants briefly handled and smelled their preferred brand of cigarette.
cigarette smoking
The three, 30-second blocks were randomized by one of three cue induction stimuli (cigarette smoking, neutral control, or cross-hair rest).

description.value: Participants viewed five cigarette-smoking-related pictures, including people smoking, smoking-related objects, and cigarettes, displayed for 24 seconds; they then rated their craving for 6 seconds.

spans.text: The 24-second cue induction stimuli contained 5 individual pictures, displayed for 4.8 seconds each.
The three, 30-second blocks were randomized by one of three cue induction stimuli (cigarette smoking, neutral control, or cross-hair rest).
neutral control

description.value: Participants viewed five pictures of people engaged in matched neutral activities or matched neutral objects such as pencils and dishes, displayed for 24 seconds; they then rated their craving for 6 seconds.

spans.text: The pictures consisted of, people smoking or engaged in matched neutral activities, and objects related to smoking (cigarettes, ashtrays, etc.) or matched neutral objects (pencils, dishes, etc.).
The three, 30-second blocks were randomized by one of three cue induction stimuli (cigarette smoking, neutral control, or cross-hair rest).
cross-hair rest

description.value: Participants viewed a cross-hair rest stimulus for 24 seconds, followed by a 6-second self-rating period.

spans.text: The three, 30-second blocks were randomized by one of three cue induction stimuli (cigarette smoking, neutral control, or cross-hair rest).
Visual stimuli were adapted from previous smoking cue fMRI studies conducted by our group ( 6 ), and were presented in a block design using standardized pictures.

stimuli.value: smoking-related and matched neutral pictures, including people smoking, cigarettes, ashtrays, pencils, and dishes

instructions.value: Participants briefly handled and smelled their preferred brand of cigarette, viewed smoking-related, neutral, or cross-hair stimuli, and rated their craving during each 6-second self-rating period using a hand-pad on a 1–5 scale.
